**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 4.2 "Termination Payment"**

Although the planner flagged this rule as likely absent, Section 4 contains a Customer-payable liquidated exit charge:

- **4.2(a)** — if *the Company* terminates, it pays HDI 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000.
- **4.2(b)** — expressly one-way: HDI never pays the Company, even where the formula is negative.
- **4.2(c)** — payable in eight quarterly instalments after termination.

Why it breaches the rule:
- Only our party pays; there is no reciprocal service credit or HDI-side remedy.
- The amount bears no relation to the fee stream (30% of Net Sales over $11,000/month), so it functions as a penalty rather than a genuine pre-estimate of loss.
- It bites on *any* Company termination — including the ordinary 90-day non-renewal right in 4.1 and termination for HDI's own breach — and on a one-year rolling term can exceed remaining contract value (a walk-away marker). Note the contrast with 1.6, which does give us a "without penalty" exit for launch failure.

Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted: delete 4.2 in full and conform the Section 4 heading to "4. Term; Termination." The comment offers the fallback — a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees, for convenience terminations only — if HDI insists on an exit charge. Separately worth raising in negotiation: there is no service-level or downtime credit regime protecting us for hosting outages.
